utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And 01970, do you recognise that one, Mr. Coo?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that as one of the Joint Command orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The same format as the others that we looked at before?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's number 74 on your list. The next ones, number 75 through 78, are also Joint Command orders, 01972, 01973, 01974, and 01977. I'm not going to show those, but just to indicate to you they are identical in format. And I will move to a different one that I want to bring up, 65 ter number 01981.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Coo, your notes indicate this was used by Mr. Milosevic in his trials in an exhibit with the witness Bozidar Delic. What can you tell us about this document? You've seen it before?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honours. This is an order from the 549th Motorised Brigade, which was one of the subordinate units of the Pristina Corps commanded by General Delic at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we go to the last page of both documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The stamp and his signature or what appears to be his signature?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is this the standard format for a VJ document of this type?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could you relate or connect the operation described in this document - if we could go back to page 1 of both English and B/C/S - can you relate or connect that to a Joint Command order?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes. If you compare the contents of this order, particularly the area that it was ordering the subunits to conduct combat operations in with one of the Joint Command orders. I don't remember which one in particular but one of the Joint Command orders at the time, it corresponds to part of that Joint Command order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, in discussions about the map you indicated that the areas you had drawn on the map were places that the Joint Command orders described as where future actions were going to take place. I want to show you 01995 and ask you a question about that. This is a document dated the 30th of March, 1999. Again, this is another one that your notes indicate came in during Mr. Milosevic's case with Defence witness General Delic. Have you seen this one before?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you'll see a reference in the first paragraph, this appears to be a post-action report describing what General Delic's brigade had done in providing support to the MUP pursuant to a Pristina Corps order. It makes reference to number 455-63 dated the 23rd of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would indicate that that document is Exhibit P350 in evidence in this case and it is a Joint Command order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: So do you need to read the rest of this or do you know what it describes in terms of the activities that were carried out by the 549?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: I recall that this was a requirement for Pristina Corps brigades to submit post-operations reports to the corps headquarters, and this is one such report. And they reported on the combat operations which had formerly taken place on the results of the operations to the corps. And this one corresponded to a large extent with the operations ordered in the Joint Command order and then subsequently ordered at a lower level by the 549 Brigade order that had been shown earlier. There's never a precise correspondence between the actual operations that take place and what's ordered in advance of the operations, but largely the correspondence between the documents was close enough to show that they were in a sequence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And is there an explanation for that lack of precise correspondence between the post-action description and the pre-action order?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: It's essentially that you can never predict what's going to happen once combat operations start. You have a plan and then you order that the combat operations should take place and you hope that the operations go according to plan, but sometimes there's -- or usually there are some differences. So for perhaps more resistance met in one village or they haven't assessed the enemy strength accurately enough and it takes longer than they originally envisaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I would like to look at 02018. This is described at number 89 in the hard copies, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Coo, this is described as an interview with General Radosavljevic, and your note indicates this was provided to the OTP by the Brook Lapping documentary company. Can you tell us what Brook Lapping was and what this interview pertained to?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: It's -- it was my understanding that Brook Lapping was a company that was commissioned by the BBC to produce a documentary on the war in Kosovo and the period preceding the NATO bombing in 1999. And this is a transcript from Brook Lapping which they provided at our request. And my understanding was that this transcript covers more than what eventually appeared in the public documentary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would indicate that the first seven pages of this interview pertain to events in 2002 and later. They're not of interest to us, but I included it to be the full transcript. We really only think from page 8 through 27 are of interest to this case, especially pages 14 and 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Next I'd like to show you 02621. This is number 94 on the list. Do you recognise that?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise that as something from the VJ web site.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: When and how was that taken from the VJ web site?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Again, I don't remember the precise date, but I checked the VJ web site during the Milosevic trial and they also produced some in English, I think, and there was a -- this public announcement by the former 3rd Army commander, General Pavkovic, commenting on issues that were relevant to the -- or issues concerning the war in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This appears to be part of what seems to be an ongoing debate or discussion between the army and the police or between Pavkovic and the Minister of the Interior, Dusan Mihajlovic, at this time, June 2001. Do you have other evidence to verify that that was going on, that there was this kind of debate or discussion taking place at that time?

utterances.speaker: PHILIP COO
utterances.text: Yes, there's -- there are a number of different sources, including contemporaneous documents from the VJ in 1999 and the issue -- the core issue here was whether or not the MUP had subordinated itself to the VJ during a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see it's time. I might have another 30 minutes, if I'm permitted. I've gone through the list, but I -- there are some VJ collegium minutes I wanted to show to Mr. Coo and ask him about. There are two items on this list that I want to withdraw because item number 2, P00998, has already been admitted in this case after it was marked by Professor Riedlmayer as, I think it's P1118. And we would also withdraw item 11 on the list, 01072, because think that was not in effect at the time of the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those two can be withdrawn, and you wish to finish tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now to continue at 9.00 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 28th day of August, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.45 p.m.,
